partner_context.their_ambition: You want to reconnect Hawaiʻi's islands without repeating the Superferry — clean, quiet inter-island mobility that respects the ocean, the whales and the communities. Pulama Lānaʻi (which stewards ~98% of Lānaʻi and Four Seasons Lānaʻi) wants frictionless, world-class access to its island; Hawaiʻi DOT Harbors carries a public mandate to move people between islands and decarbonize.
partner_context.their_pressure: The 2007–2009 Hawaii Superferry was killed by wake, whale-strike and environmental-review objections, leaving you with no inter-island ferry and total dependence on air. Road congestion on Oʻahu is among the worst in the US, and your state carries aggressive clean-transportation targets.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: A foiling hull flies clear of the water — quiet, low-wake, zero-emission — the direct answer to every objection that grounded the Superferry. Navier reconnects your islands the way Hawaiʻi wished the Superferry had, and gives Pulama Lānaʻi a signature all-electric arrival experience.

hero.eyebrow: Authority proposal · State of Hawaiʻi · DOT Harbors
hero.title: Hawaiʻi × Navier — the Superferry, done right
hero.subtitle: Quiet, low-wake, zero-emission foiling — the inter-island connection Hawaiʻi has been missing since 2009.
hero.what_we_do_together: We start with Pulama Lānaʻi: an all-electric foiling arrival to Four Seasons Lānaʻi across the sheltered ʻAuʻau Channel — a signature experience a private island owner can launch fast. Then we scale into the public inter-island network with Hawaiʻi DOT Harbors: Honolulu ↔ Molokaʻi, the ʻAlenuihāhā seasickness-relief crossing, and the Maui/Kauaʻi line-hauls — clean and quiet enough to clear the review that stopped the Superferry.

why_now: Hawaii has had no scheduled inter-island ferry since the Superferry shut down in 2009 — proven latent demand (300k+ passengers carried in under two years) with no clean way to serve it. Navier's software-defined foiling vessels lift clear of the water, eliminating the wake and whale-strike concerns that grounded the incumbent, and the Quanta-LR hybrid (commercial H2 2026+) needs no charging infrastructure at the outer harbors. Foiling is culturally native to the Pacific sailing world — the America's Cup connection makes 'is this proven?' an easy objection to answer.
multimodal_fit: Pioneer II all-electric owns the short sheltered channels (Maui↔Lānaʻi ~9 nm, Maui↔Molokaʻi ~8 nm, Honolulu↔Molokaʻi ~25 nm) and the Kona–Kohala resort coast; the Quanta-LR hybrid carries the inter-island line-hauls (Honolulu↔Maui ~75 nm, Honolulu↔Kauaʻi ~72 nm) with no charging dependency. Door-to-door it pairs with rideshare and resort transfers at each harbor.

differentiation.why_navier: Software-defined, autonomy-ready, zero-emission and low-wake by design — the only vessel profile that answers the exact objections that grounded your Superferry, with a hybrid option that needs no charging at the outer harbors.

proof_points.claim: The latent inter-island demand is proven.
proof_points.evidence: Hawaii Superferry carried 300k+ passengers in under two years before its environmental-review shutdown.

proof_points.claim: The network model is real and at scale.
The technology is delivered and proven.
proof_points.evidence: 10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out.

objections.concern: Isn't this just the Superferry again?
objections.response: The opposite. The Superferry was a large diesel catamaran whose wake and whale-strike risk failed environmental review. A Navier foiling hull flies clear of the water — low-wake, quiet, zero-emission — which is precisely what that review was asking for.

objections.concern: What about the channels — aren't they too rough?
objections.response: That is the point. ʻAlenuihāhā is among the roughest channels on Earth, and a foiling hull that cancels the chop turns the worst crossing in Hawaii into the smoothest — the strongest comfort story in the portfolio.

objections.concern: What about charging at the outer islands?
objections.response: Pioneer II all-electric covers the short sheltered channels from main harbors; the Quanta-LR hybrid carries the longer line-hauls with no charging infrastructure required at Molokaʻi, Lānaʻi or Kauaʻi.

phases.label: Today's crossing, upgraded
phases.narrative: The live Maui–Lānaʻi ferry, flown clear of the water — the same sheltered ʻAuʻau Channel crossing Hawaiʻi already runs, now faster, quieter, whale-safe and zero-emission.

phases.label: Reconnecting the main islands
phases.narrative: The statewide inter-island service Hawaiʻi has lacked since 2009 — Oʻahu to Molokaʻi and Maui, and the Maui-County connectors — restored on low-wake foils that clear the bar the Superferry could not.

phases.label: The full inter-island network
phases.narrative: The longest, roughest channels last — the ʻAlenuihāhā crossing to Hawaiʻi Island and the Kauaʻi line-haul — the crossings a foiling hull turns from the worst rides in Hawaiʻi into the smoothest.

the_ask.navier_brings: Software-defined, zero-emission, low-wake foiling vessels and network operations — the only profile that answers the Superferry objections.
the_ask.partner_brings: You bring the pieces: Pulama Lānaʻi brings the signature island and the fast first launch; Hawaiʻi DOT Harbors brings the berths, the public mandate and the inter-island network.
the_ask.next_step: A Pulama-Lānaʻi-anchored Phase 1 arrival to Four Seasons Lānaʻi, with a parallel DOT Harbors conversation on the inter-island network.

close.title: The connection Hawaiʻi has been missing since 2009.
close.body: Start with a signature all-electric arrival to Lānaʻi, prove the channel comfort and the clean-and-quiet case, then reconnect the islands the way the Superferry never could.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop — roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother, quieter and lower-wake. It is software-defined and autonomy-ready. A step-change in marine mobility, not an incremental faster boat — and the exact profile Hawaii's environmental review was asking for.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on the open ocean and the harbors already in use. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all — so the outer islands (Molokaʻi, Lānaʻi, Kauaʻi) need nothing built to be connected.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Hawaii has had no inter-island ferry for over fifteen years despite proven demand; decarbonization mandates now favor zero-emission marine; the hybrid removes the outer-island charging excuse; and foiling is culturally native to the Pacific. The window to reconnect the islands cleanly is open now.

end_state.headline: Inter-island mobility for Hawaiʻi — the Superferry, done right.
end_state.addressable_footprint: All six main Hawaiian Islands under a Pulama Lānaʻi + Hawaiʻi DOT Harbors anchor — Oʻahu, Maui, Hawaiʻi Island, Kauaʻi, Lānaʻi and Molokaʻi — wherever residents and visitors fly today because the sea crossing is rough, slow or wake-restricted.

steady_state.platform_mix: Pioneer II for Maui↔Lānaʻi and short hops; Quanta-LR for Oʻahu↔Maui↔Hawaiʻi Island channel crossings
steady_state.the_opportunity: Every inter-island trip today is a flight or it doesn't happen; quiet, low-wake foiling answers the exact objections that killed the 2009 Superferry and reopens the sea as a mode.

end_state.narrative: Steady state is the sea crossing Hawaiʻi lost: a quiet, low-wake foiling network that clears the environmental and community objections the 2009 Superferry never could, with Lānaʻi as the proof and DOT Harbors as the spine.
